name: Saudi Awwal Bank
legal_name: Saudi Awwal Bank (a Saudi Joint Stock Company); formerly The Saudi British Bank (SABB), renamed effective 11 June 2023
founded: 1978 (Royal Decree M/4 dated 21 Jan 1978; took over The British Bank of the Middle East's Saudi operations on 1 Jul 1978). Merged with Alawwal Bank in June 2019; renamed from The Saudi British Bank to Saudi Awwal Bank effective 11 Jun 2023.
ownership_summary: Listed on Tadawul. HSBC Holdings B.V. holds 636,986,300 shares (31%) and Olayan Saudi Investment Company Ltd holds 422,208,905 shares (20.55%) at 31 Dec 2025 (AR 2025). The AR's market page shows the Olayan family at 20.6% and total foreign ownership at 46.8%. HSBC appoints three of the eleven directors under the bylaws. A technical services agreement with HSBC Holdings plc was renewed for 10 years from 30 Sep 2017.
government_link: No controlling government shareholder disclosed. The two shareholders above 5% are HSBC Holdings B.V. (31%) and Olayan Saudi Investment Company (20.55%) at 31 Dec 2025 (S4).
group_structure: Parent bank with 100%-owned subsidiaries: Alawwal Invest Company, trading as SAB Invest (CMA-licensed brokerage, asset management, advisory, custody; profiled separately as sa-sab-invest), Arabian Real Estate Company (ARECO), Alawwal Real Estate Company (AREC), SAB Markets Limited (Cayman; derivatives and repo) and the X-Tech fund (private equity fund managed by SAB Invest). SAB also holds 49% of HSBC Saudi Arabia, an associate and separate CMA-licensed investment bank (HSBC Group holds the other 51%), which is not consolidated (S3 note 1). The bank reports a 'Capital markets' segment that brings together SAB Invest's brokerage, margin lending and asset management (S4). Double counting: SAB Invest's assets, revenue and AUM are consolidated into SAB's figures and its Capital markets segment. Do not add sa-sab-invest metrics to this record.

footprint: Saudi Arabia only. 101 branches at 30 Jun 2026 (100 at 31 Dec 2025) (S3 note 1). 999 ATMs at end-2025 (S4). Private Banking centres in Riyadh, Jeddah and Al Khobar (S10).
customer_segments: Retail mass market; affluent propositions Advance, Premier and Top Tier (AR 2025); Private Banking (HNW/UHNW); international customers (47% of the client base) and affluent customers (17%) per AR 2025; SME; corporate and institutional (over 35k clients). More than 1.7 million retail customers at end-2025 (S4).
business_lines: Segments (S3 note 17): Wealth and Personal Banking (WPB; retail, affluent, Private Banking, cards, mortgages), Corporate and Institutional Banking, Treasury, Capital markets (SAB Invest brokerage, margin lending and asset management) and Others (associate). H1 2026 total operating income SAR 7,275.0m: WPB 2,043.6m, CIB 3,999.4m, Treasury 1,061.4m, Capital markets 185.2m (S3). The bank offers Shariah-compliant products under an independent Shariah Committee. The 49%-owned HSBC Saudi Arabia covers investment banking.

capabilities.wealth_summary: SAB runs wealth through its Wealth and Personal Banking (WPB) unit, led by Chief Wealth & Personal Banking Officer Bandar Al-Gheshayan, with investment products supplied by its 100% subsidiary SAB Invest (legal name Alawwal Invest Company). Affluent propositions are Advance, Premier and Top Tier. SAB Premier mirrors HSBC Premier: entry is a SAR 40,000 monthly salary, a SAR 500,000 3-month average balance (or SAR 750,000 combined with SAB Invest), SAR 1m initial balance, SAR 3m home finance, or an existing HSBC Premier relationship. Private Banking has centres in Riyadh, Jeddah and Al Khobar and won Euromoney's Best Private Bank in Saudi Arabia for a fourth year in 2026. Referrals from SAB to SAB Invest reached SAR 4.7bn in 2025, three times the previous three years combined, and Euromoney says almost 80% of private bank clients invest via SAB Invest. The SAB mobile app itself shows no investing; investing runs in SAB Invest's apps, including a new Digital Wealth app with the 'MAL' robo/model-portfolio service (soft-launched 2025) and the WorldTrader global brokerage platform. The bank's 2021-2026 strategy ends in 2026 and management said on 9 Feb 2026 that the next 4-5 year plan is being prepared this year.

private_banking.detail: Private Banking within WPB: dedicated RMs, centres in Riyadh, Jeddah and Al Khobar, lending solutions, portfolios built through SAB Invest's public and private products, and free SAB-HSBC Global View/Global Transfer (S10). AR 2025: Private Banking assets more than doubled since the 2019 merger and deposits rose over 1.5 times; referrals from SAB to SAB Invest totalled SAR 4.7bn in 2025 (S4). Euromoney (Mar 2026): deposits +14% in 9M 2025 and almost 80% of private bank clients invest via Alawwal Invest (S18). Euromoney Best Private Banking in Saudi Arabia for the fourth consecutive year, plus Global Finance Best Private Banking (14 Apr 2026, S14). SAB Invest also reports transactions executed with HSBC Private Banking in 2025 (see sa-sab-invest).

asset_management.detail: Through SAB Invest (100%): AUM SAR 34,176m at end-2025 (SAR 35,044m end-2024), of which SAR 3.4bn in Global Investment Solutions. Conventional and Shariah mutual funds, multi-asset funds, DPMs, real estate, private credit and VC funds, and ETFs (Saudi Quant ETF built with HSBC Asset Management; Hang Seng Hong Kong ETF). See sa-sab-invest.

brokerage.detail: Through SAB Invest: Saudi, GCC and international equities; margin lending; WorldTrader international platform (50+ exchanges, US options) launched 2025. Capital markets segment operating income SAR 185.2m in H1 2026 (-10% YoY). HSBC Saudi Arabia (49% associate) handles institutional equities and investment banking.

digital_investing.detail: Investing sits in SAB Invest's channels, not the SAB banking app: SAB Invest app (fund investing; first iOS release 31 Dec 2025), SAB Invest Trade, WorldTrader and WorldTrader Pro, SAB Invest Online. SAB's mobile app is used to open the USD account that funds WorldTrader. AR 2025 reports digital users at 93% of active customers and asset digital sales at 31% of total sales, but no in-app investing in the SAB app was found.

advisory.detail: Premier RMs give 'specialist advice' on financial planning and investments (S11). SAB Invest Global Investment Solutions provides advisory and Outsourced CIO services; assets under advisory surpassed SAR 2.9bn at end-2025 (S4).

discretionary.detail: SAB Invest discretionary portfolio management (DPMs) for HNW, affluent, corporate and institutional clients (see sa-sab-invest).

model_portfolios_robo.detail: Via SAB Invest: 'MAL - Mustasharak Alawwal' in the new Digital Wealth app offers one-off or systematic investment into model portfolios managed by SAB Invest and rebalanced by a robo engine; soft-launched in 2025 per the SAB Invest board report (see sa-sab-invest). Not offered inside the SAB bank app.

funds_platform.detail: Wealth management page lists SAB Invest mutual funds (equities and money markets, domestic and overseas) as the bank's investment shelf (S13). No third-party fund platform found at the bank. SAB Invest is listing its own funds with HSBC's booking centre for foreign investors (see sa-sab-invest).

structured_products.detail: No retail structured products on the bank's wealth pages. Treasury commercialised equity derivatives on local and international stocks for clients in 2025 (S4). SAB Invest lists structured products among asset management capabilities and offers 'Save+', a structured savings product (see sa-sab-invest).

private_markets.detail: Through SAB Invest: real estate development funds, the first MENA private credit strategy for clients, global private credit funds, a Shariah venture income fund with STV, and the X-Tech VC fund consolidated by the bank (S3, S4).

islamic_wealth.detail: Shariah-compliant products under an independent Shariah Committee (S3 note 1); Islamic Mudaraba savings and commodity investment accounts on the wealth page (S13); Shariah funds and Shariah-compliant global credit fund at SAB Invest.

partners.what: 31% shareholder; technical services agreement with HSBC Holdings plc renewed for 10 years from 30 Sep 2017; HSBC Premier recognition; Global View & Global Transfer across 18 corridors (SAR 5.3bn transfers for 8,500 customers since launch); collaboration on digital assets and AI; WPB priority to implement HSBC's customer lifecycle management (CLCM)
Supplies funds, DPMs, brokerage, robo/model portfolios and private markets to bank clients; SAR 4.7bn referrals in 2025
